en: Dependent on a state that is not associated with taints (*anāsava*), not visible (*anidassana*), and non-reactive (*appaṭigha*), there arises a state associated with taints, visible, and reactive, by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*) … one.

Dependent on a state that is not associated with taints, not visible, and non-reactive, there arises a state associated with taints, visible, and reactive, by way of root condition … one. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are three; under predominance condition there are three … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are three.

(There are three questions for the root that is not associated with the outflows (*anāsava*), not visible (*anidassana*), and non-reactive (*appaṭigha*), according to the previous method. With respect to the root condition (*hetu*), there are three; with respect to the predominance condition (*adhipati*), there are three ... [and so on] ... with respect to the mutuality condition (*aññamañña*), there is one ... [and so on] ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*), there are three.

Dependent on a state that is not associated with the outflows, not visible, and non-reactive, there arises a state associated with the outflows (*sāsava*), not visible, and non-reactive, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. With respect to the root condition, there is one; with respect to the predominance condition, there is one ... [and so on] ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition, there is one.
